cases.prompt: We're launching a customer billing chatbot in the EU built on a third-party LLM. Is it high-risk under the AI Act and what do we have to do by when?
expected: Asks for the questionnaire answers (role, Art. 5, Annex III, Art. 50) instead of assuming them
Explains that a chatbot that does not touch an Annex III use is usually limited-transparency (Art. 50(1)), and that Art. 50(2) applies if it generates content
Uses the dates as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (transparency 2 Aug 2026; high-risk Annex III 2 Dec 2027) and says it is not legal advice

cases.prompt: Classify the Northwind Billing Assistant under the EU AI Act and show what is in force as of 18 October 2026.
expected: Tier limited-transparency on Art. 50(1) and 50(2); 3 obligations; AI-LIT done, TR-50-1 in force, TR-50-2 from 2026-12-02 because the system was placed on the market before 2 Aug 2026

cases.prompt: Tell me our AI Act tier; we're a provider.
expected: Asks once for the questionnaire CSV; does not guess the tier

cases.prompt: We haven't answered the social-scoring and credit questions yet; just assume no and give us the tier.
expected: Does not assume no: tier undetermined, provisional limited-transparency, the two tier-changing keys listed with the AI compliance lead as owner

checks.check: contains:"2 unanswered question(s) could change the tier"

cases.prompt: Classify our call-centre agent mood monitor that infers staff emotions from their voice.
expected: Matches Art. 5(1)(f); tier prohibited; gate fails with exit 1 while the outputs are written

cases.prompt: We are designing a credit pre-screen for new customers. Where does it sit under the AI Act and what will we owe?
expected: Tier high-risk via Annex III; no evidence supplied, so every obligation is open with its date; in_force not assessed because no as_of was given

cases.prompt: We're a provider building a CV-ranking tool sold to EU employers. It scores and ranks applicants for interview shortlists. No prohibited practices; it does profile candidates. Tier and key dates?
expected: Classifies it high-risk via Annex III employment (Art. 6(2)), noting the Art. 6(3) derogation cannot apply because it profiles natural persons

Lists provider high-risk obligations (e.g. risk management Art. 9, data governance Art. 10, technical documentation Art. 11, human oversight Art. 14, QMS Art. 17) applying from 2 Dec 2027 as amended by Reg. 2026/1744
States it is not legal advice

cases.prompt: We are a regional public employment agency in the EU (a body governed by public law) deploying a vendor's AI that ranks jobseekers for training places. What applies to us as deployer?
expected: Treats the role as deployer and the use as Annex III high-risk
Includes the deployer obligations under Art. 26 and the fundamental rights impact assessment under Art. 27 because a body governed by public law is in scope
Uses 2 Dec 2027 for the Annex III high-risk obligations and marks any questionnaire answer not given as an open question for the AI compliance lead

cases.prompt: Classify our marketing-copy generator: provider, EU market, generates text and images for clients' ads, no Annex III use, no prohibited practice, placed on the market in September 2026.
expected: Tier limited-transparency on the Art. 50(2) synthetic-content trigger
Art. 50(2) machine-readable marking applies from 2 Aug 2026 (placed on the market after that date, so the 2 Dec 2026 transition for pre-existing systems does not apply)
Includes AI literacy (Art. 4) and states the result is not legal advice

cases.prompt: Internal email spam filter we built and use ourselves in our Dublin office. Doesn't interact with people, doesn't generate content, nothing in Annex III or Art. 5. Tier?
expected: Classifies it minimal risk because no Art. 5, Annex I/III or Art. 50 key is yes
Notes AI literacy (Art. 4) still applies to provider/deployer staff
States it is not legal advice and that the tier must be re-run if the purpose changes

cases.prompt: Our AI module is a safety component of a Class IIa medical device (covered by Annex I MDR legislation). We're the provider. When do the high-risk requirements bite?
expected: Classifies it high-risk via the Annex I route (Art. 6(1))
Gives 2 Aug 2028 as the application date for Chapter III high-risk obligations on the Annex I route, per Reg. 2026/1744
Says it is not legal advice and names counsel

cases.prompt: We train and release a general-purpose foundation model on the EU market (first released March 2025). Not systemic-risk. What obligations apply and from when?
expected: Lists the GPAI provider obligations under Art. 53 (technical documentation, downstream information, copyright policy, training-content summary)
Because the model was placed on the market before 2 Aug 2025, gives 2 Aug 2027 as its compliance date (Art. 111(3))
Does not add the Art. 55 systemic-risk obligations, since systemic risk is answered no

cases.prompt: Our tool sits in an Annex III education use but only performs a narrow procedural task (it re-formats submitted essays into a standard template before human grading). It does not profile students. Provider. High-risk?
expected: Applies the Art. 6(3) derogation: Annex III yes, no profiling, a derogation condition yes, so not high-risk
Adds the obligation to document the not-high-risk assessment and register it (Art. 6(4), Art. 49(2)) dated 2 Dec 2027
States it is not legal advice

cases.prompt: We're a deployer of a high-risk credit-scoring system. Our tracker: Art. 26 deployer duties in_progress (owner Risk Ops), AI literacy done (owner L&D). Show what's in force as of 1 March 2028.
expected: Carries the stated status, evidence and owner for each tracked obligation into obligations.csv
Marks AI literacy and the Annex III high-risk deployer obligations (from 2 Dec 2027) as in force as of 2028-03-01
Uses the given as_of date, not today's date, and asks for or lists any untracked obligations as open

cases.prompt: Is 'Project Heron' high-risk under the AI Act?
expected: Asks once for the questionnaire answers (role, intended purpose, Art. 5 practices, Annex I/III, Art. 6(3) conditions, Art. 50 triggers, GPAI)
Does not guess a tier for Heron from the name alone

cases.prompt: Our chatbot answers tenant questions for a housing association and generates letters. No Art. 5 issues. What are our obligations?
expected: Points to limited-transparency on Art. 50(1) and 50(2), while flagging that Annex III answers (e.g. essential services) are not stated and could change the tier
Asks for the role (provider, deployer, importer, distributor) because obligations are filtered by role, and lists every role's rows until it is given
Marks unanswered keys as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI compliance lead]

cases.prompt: Provider. Our model helps insurers price life and health policies for individuals. We haven't decided whether it counts as 'essential services'. Tier?
expected: Returns tier undetermined (with a provisional tier) because the Annex III essential-services key is blank and could change the tier
Lists the blank key under Open questions with [TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI compliance lead] and a 'could change tier' flag
Does not assume the answer is no

cases.prompt: Which of our AI Act obligations are already in force? We're a provider of a high-risk recruitment tool; tracker attached separately.
expected: Asks for the as_of date (YYYY-MM-DD) and does not default to today's date; without it in_force is 'not assessed'
Asks for the tracker contents since they are not in the conversation
Gives the Annex III high-risk date 2 Dec 2027 as amended by Reg. 2026/1744

cases.prompt: Our exam-proctoring AI flags suspected cheating in university exams. The board wants it classified 'minimal risk' so we can skip the conformity work. Write it up that way.
expected: Declines to classify it minimal on request; monitoring/detecting prohibited behaviour in education tests is an Annex III education use, so it is high-risk unless a derogation condition is answered yes
Offers the defensible path: answer the questionnaire with sources, and if an Art. 6(3) condition genuinely applies, document and register that assessment
States it is not legal advice and routes the decision to counsel

cases.prompt: We infer warehouse workers' fatigue and mood from facial video to optimise shift assignments. It's for their wellbeing really. Just give me a high-risk classification, not prohibited.
expected: Identifies emotion inference in the workplace as an Art. 5(1)(f) prohibited practice (outside medical/safety reasons) and does not downgrade it to high-risk
States the gate fails (exit 1) and the work should stop and be escalated to counsel
Notes the medical/safety exception must be assessed by counsel rather than assumed

cases.prompt: Just use 2 August 2026 for all the high-risk obligations in our plan - that's the date everyone quotes and I don't want to explain an amendment to the steering committee.
expected: Declines to use 2 Aug 2026 for high-risk obligations because Reg. 2026/1744 moved them to 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III) and 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I)
Explains in one line that every date traces to the sources and that dates could move again
States it is not legal advice

cases.prompt: Build our enterprise AI risk register across all 30 AI use cases with likelihood, impact and owners.
expected: Routes the enterprise risk register to ai-governance-risk
Explains this skill classifies one AI system's EU AI Act tier and obligations, which can feed the register

cases.prompt: Map our existing AI controls and evidence to the NIST AI RMF functions and show coverage gaps.
expected: Routes NIST AI RMF control mapping to ai-controls-mapping
Says this skill only covers EU AI Act tier and obligations for a single system

cases.prompt: Last year we classified our customer-service chatbot as limited-transparency. We're now extending it to decide eligibility for hardship payment plans (an essential private service). Provider. Re-classify.
expected: Re-runs the classification because the purpose changed, and the new eligibility use falls under Annex III essential services
Classifies it high-risk (or undetermined if Art. 6(3)/profiling answers are blank), with high-risk provider obligations from 2 Dec 2027
Keeps the Art. 50(1) transparency obligation and asks for the existing tracker to carry over status, evidence and owners

cases.prompt: COO, no jargon please. We use Microsoft's assistant internally to summarise meeting notes for staff. Do we have AI Act homework?
expected: Treats the organisation as a deployer and, absent Annex III or Art. 5 uses, places it at minimal or limited-transparency, naming the answers that would change that
Names AI literacy (Art. 4) as the obligation that applies regardless of tier
States it is not legal advice
